title: Source, build and execution
goal: Identify the stage at which a program changes. Fix a build error first, then fix its behaviour.

prerequisites.text: You can distinguish the program text from the text displayed in the result area.

terms.title: Compilation
terms.definition: Translating the source after checking the rules of the language.

terms.title: Linking
terms.definition: Joining translated code with the implementations it needs, such as puts from the library.

terms.title: Execution
terms.definition: Running the program after a successful build.

sections.title: One click, several stages
paragraphs: When a control panel says Sensor ready, you see the result of running a program. First there was the main.c source file, then the environment prepared a program, then it ran it. Editing the text does not by itself change previous output.

In practice a build handles inclusions, compilation and linking. Code Studio starts these actions with one click and runs C17 via Clang/WASI. The names of the stages help you tell where the operation stopped.
The builder checks whether it can translate the source. It does not know whether you need ready or waiting. That requires predicting and comparing the program result.

sections.title: The sensor is ready
paragraphs: Open main.c. Before running, name the source file and the expected output line. After running, find the result separately from the build messages.
steps: When building, the compiler sees a complete call statement terminated by a semicolon. The build prepares the program for execution.
On execution, puts writes the line. Only now does Sensor ready appear on stdout.
trace: puts wrote the line to stdout

sections.title: Two different failures
paragraphs: Make a copy and remove the ; after puts. The compiler reports malformed syntax and that run produces no new program output. Exact wording depends on the Clang version. Reinsert the ; and run again.
Now keep the syntax valid but replace ready with waiting. The build can succeed. Comparing the output with the goal reveals the wrong text.

sections.title: Build first, then compare
paragraphs: The new status starter has two different problems. Fix one thing at a time to see which problem each edit resolves.
Do not stop at the first successful build. Check the exact output, including the colon and the space following it.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Defines the translation stages and diagnostic requirements.

selfcheck.prompt: After a successful build and run, what goes to stdout?
feedback: Correct. The executed call writes only the message.
The declaration is used at build time.
The source is edited rather than copied to stdout.

selfcheck.prompt: The compiler reports a missing ;. What does this run produce?
options: Fresh output with the previous text
No new program output because the build stopped
feedback: Correct. The new version cannot run yet.
A successfully built program can print.

selfcheck.prompt: How do you tell a build error from a program that builds successfully but reports the wrong status?
selfcheck.feedback: With a build error, fix the source using the diagnostic and rebuild. After a successful run, compare the status that actually printed with the requirement.

practice.title: Build a status indicator
practice.task: Edit the starter main.c until a successful run prints Status: ready. Fix the build with waiting unchanged first. Record what happens, then edit the message.

cases.label: After the syntax and text fixes

criteria: After the first change, it builds and prints Status: waiting.
After the second change, stdout contains only Status: ready.
You can explain each error separately.
practice.hint: The puts call needs a terminating ;. The message is between quotes.

steps.expected: There is a build diagnostic and no new stdout line.
The build succeeds and Status: waiting appears.

steps.action: Replace waiting with ready and repeat.
steps.why: Now you are checking execution rather than syntax.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: In a copy of your finished program, remove the closing quote temporarily. Record the stage where it stops, restore the quote and change the message to Status: offline.
criteria: Name the stage of each check and compare the final output with the prediction.

teaching.scene: A panel should show that its sensor is ready. Locate the build and the later appearance of fresh output separately. This tells you which step prevented the display from updating.

predict.prompt: The sample source contains puts. After which action does its line appear, and what does that line say?
predict.answer: The environment first compiles the source and links the program with the functions it uses. Running the result reaches puts, which writes Sensor ready. Build success makes execution possible, and stdout confirms the text.

apply.prompt: An alarm panel still shows its old message after a run with a syntax error. Which two observations tell you when the new message really appears?
apply.answer: Look for a build diagnostic and the absence of fresh output after the error. Once the repaired program runs, compare the new line with the panel requirement.

practice.strategy: First fix the diagnostic and rerun with waiting intact. Once you have verified the first output, change the message and run again.
practice.diagnosis: The compiler message points to the source before execution. Seeing waiting after the repair confirms that the build now succeeds and the text still needs updating.

syntax.explanation: The compiler must parse the source as a call with an argument followed by `;`. Execution reaches the call after a successful build and run.
syntax.mistake: A missing `;` after the call stops the build. Inspect the end of the call in the first reported area.
